subject: english-literature
title: Cultural Moment
welcome_lead: Every text emerges from and addresses a specific cultural moment. Understanding the moment lets you read the text's interventions.
meta_desc: English Literature: cultural and political contexts shaping literary meaning.
final_note: A text speaks to its moment — and asks us to listen across time.

concepts.def: The defining spirit or mood of a particular period of history.
The intersection of political, social, and artistic forces at a specific time.
How a text has been read and valued by successive audiences.
The body of texts traditionally regarded as authoritative within a literary tradition.
Dividing literary history into periods such as Romantic, Modernist, Postmodern.
The historical conditions of book production and circulation.

walkthroughs.body_html: The 1920s Modernism of Eliot and Woolf responds to the trauma of WWI. The fragmented forms are not arbitrary — they enact a fractured worldview.
Victorian readers found Wuthering Heights shocking and crude; today it is canonical. Reception history reveals how literary value is constructed.
When does Modernism begin — 1900? 1910? 1922? Periods are heuristic, not natural. Be precise about which features define a movement.

mcqs.q: What is the structure of a Shakespearean sonnet?
options: A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
Fourteen lines in iambic pentameter, structured as three quatrains and a final couplet, rhyming ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, often with a volta near the couplet.
A sonnet is any short love poem.
The speaker is whoever reads the poem out loud.

mcqs.q: Why distinguish the speaker of a poem from the poet?
options: The speaker of a poem is always the poet themselves.
A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
The speaker is whoever reads the poem out loud.
The speaker is the voice constructed in the poem; the poet is the writer. Treating them as identical can mislead, especially with dramatic monologues or personae.
The speaker is whoever reads the poem out loud.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
Pathetic fallacy is when an argument in a story is weak or sad.
Attributing human emotions or qualities to nature or inanimate objects to reflect a character's feelings or scene's mood (e.g. angry storms during conflict).
